chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to His servants. He is more Knowing of what is in the breasts, and more Seeing of what is in the eyes. He is closer to them than the jugular vein. He does good to the doers of good, and repays for goodness. He does good to the doers of good among His creation with His mercy, and punishes the doers of evil with His justice. And his Lord does not wrong anyone.

key_terms.الصُّدُور: the breasts (hearts/chests, referring to inner thoughts)
key_terms.حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ: the jugular vein (a measure of closeness)

ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of Allah regarding justice and mercy in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this hadith within the Shia doctrine of *Adl* (Divine Justice), affirming that Allah’s mercy and justice are intrinsic to His essence rather than arbitrary decrees. It underscores the theological principle that divine recompense is perfectly balanced, ensuring that no soul bears the burden of another, a key tenet distinguishing Shia thought from other schools regarding predestination and free will.
